To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) microfinance is a new financial technology that has been developed to support the neoliberal Washington Consensus; (ii) the microfinance industry is growing rapidly and is becoming increasingly global in its scope and reach; and (iii) microfinance may be used by the Washington Consensus to promote the privatization of social services, the commodification of human services and the commercialization of social relations.

the microfinance institutions (MFIs) that we studied in India, Bangladesh, Bolivia, and Peru have not been successful in reducing poverty.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the "Washington Consensus" is a set of policies that has been used in many developing countries to encourage economic development and growth.
microfinance is an excellent way to help the poor, but not a way to end global poverty.
the Washington Consensus is a set of policy recommendations for developing countries, which are not always followed, but are still a useful guide for economic policy makers in developing countries.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
microfinance is not the panacea it is made out to be.
microfinance has become a new form of financial technology of the Washington Consaensus.
the microfinance industry is a "new technology", but not a "new financial technology".
The main takeaway from our work is that
microfinance may be an effective tool for the development of poor communities but it is not a panacea for the poverty problem.
microfinance may be the latest in the series of new financial technologies of the Washington Consasensus, and it may be the most problematic.
the microfinance industry is not as "poor" as it is made out to be.
